history.subject: Map: Add support for Ionosonde stations

hypothesis.leading_explanation: An image editor or export path overwrote a larger PNG without truncating it, potentially across multiple successive saves.
evidence: The current image ends at byte 4154; two more valid empty IEND chunks end at bytes 5379 and 73152.
Large residues resemble compressed binary data and end in a PNG terminator, with no validated program or archive recovered.
Related SDRangel icons antennadab.png, antennafm.png and antennatime.png have exact shared residual suffixes at identical absolute offsets.
The identical full PNG was present at its initial upstream introduction in 2022.
hypothesis.confidence: Likely accidental image-export residue; the exact original larger image and editor are not proven.
hypothesis.does_not_establish: Upstream provenance alone does not certify safety; suspicious anomaly severity remains appropriate.

access_paths.behavior: Bundles map/ionosonde.png as a Qt resource.
Sets an ionosonde station map item image to the literal filename.
Exposes the image filename as mapImage.
Qt Image.source consumes mapImage; same path in map_6.qml and legacy map_5_12.qml.
Emits the filename as a Cesium billboard image URL.
QResource reads all resource bytes and sendFile sends them as image/png. Does not trim the trailer. QFile::readAll is a generic fallback, not a special icon reader.

direct_read_conclusion: No application-specific PNG or trailer decoder was found. It would be incorrect to say SDRangel never reads the bytes: its generic resource server reads and serves the entire file. No offset seek, bit-plane extraction, script evaluation or payload execution tied to this image was found. This is a static source review of v7.22.5, not an absolute proof covering all third-party runtime components.
classification: Keep the PNG suspicious for its >=64 KiB opaque trailer. The parent package remains inconclusive because the exact original content of the large residual region has not been established, although source and history strongly favor an accidental image-export artifact. No malicious decoding behavior was identified.
